summary: Hand-coded regex extractors for text properties were checked against sample labels; seven properties split every probe's labels perfectly and became candidates. Per-latent attribution c = gradient x (label1-label0 mean shift) was computed on 32+32 sample notes per probe; latents were assigned to property/topic groups by matching their cross-probe sign pattern of mean shifts to templates, confirmed with corpus top examples. Group contribution sums picked the cue per probe. True-logit texts went to one hand-written pair per probe flipping all seven properties together, to measure total property dependence; a negative difference gave 'none'. Latent sets were assembled from template-matched, example-confirmed latents, checked by SAE ablation on sample notes; regexes were single-marker patterns checked for balanced accuracy on sample notes.

phases.purpose: Inspect sample/corpus files; build regex extractors for 16 text properties; find the seven perfectly label-split properties and check their independence in the corpus
Select 32 notes per label per probe; get gradients and mean activations; compute per-latent contribution g*delta

Pool top-14 latents per probe; build corpus topic/property labels; characterise candidates by trigger tokens and topic fractions; match cross-probe delta signs to property/topic templates; sum contributions per hand-classified group
Ablate all 20 property-classified latents on sample notes to compare SAE gap before/after
One hand-written pair per probe flipping all seven properties together while keeping topic content, to measure total property dependence including the SAE error term

Assign all latents to templates by cosine; split the list/british/ps sign-degenerate group via trigger tokens; sum contributions of verified clean latents per property; examine gender/tense candidates for probe 2
Attempted pooled regression of SAE logit on properties plus topic dummies (abandoned for collinearity); search for spelling latents (abandoned)
Collect template-matched candidates for hashtag, list and exclamation cues; confirm extra latents by examples; check on-sample ablation removal; keep positive-contribution list latents
Check regex balanced accuracy on sample notes; search for more hashtag latents; validate and submit answer

per_probe.procedure: Top contributors by g*delta (2170, 15434, 1282, 10695, 4373) matched the hashtag sign template and triggered on '#' or hashtag words in corpus examples. Hashtag group sum dominated probe 0 (template-group and verified-latent sums), and the all-properties-flipped true-logit pair gave a large difference. Latent set: hashtag-template candidates ranked by |c0|, extra ones (14657, 12323, 2767) confirmed by '#new'/'tivity'/'metime' triggers; on-sample ablation removed part of the gap. A further search found no more clean hashtag latents. Regex '#', balanced accuracy checked on sample notes.
per_probe.quote: Big insight forming: probe 0's top contributors (2170, 15434, 1282, 10695, 4373) are **all hashtag latents** (trigger "#" / "#positivity", d-pattern matches hash template).

per_probe.procedure: Contributions were dominated by fishing topic latents (12110). The hand-written pair flipping all seven properties together gave a negative true-logit difference (label-0-side properties scored higher), read as no property dependence. Answered none.

The flip-all pair showed large property dependence, but no clean group stood out: the list/british/ps group shared a sign template and was split by trigger tokens into bullet latents ('-') and P.S. latents. Verified sums for list, ps and excl were all small; gender/tense latents had the wrong sign, spelling latents were small. List was chosen by elimination because it was the most coherent group with the strongest single latent (6261). Latents: list-template candidates by |c2|, confirmed by '-' triggers, keeping positive c2 only. Regex '(?m)^- '.
per_probe.quote: By elimination for probe2: gender is wrong-sign, tense incoherent, hashtag/excl/spelling tiny — leaving LIST (coherent, strongest single latent 6261) as the cue.

per_probe.procedure: Latent 11837 fired on '!' in corpus examples and matched the exclamation sign template; the exclamation group dominated probe 3's contribution sums. The true-logit pair was built with the punctuation flipped the wrong way, so the decision rested on latent contributions. Latents: excl/period template candidates ranked by |c3| (11837, 14647, 14728) plus 6482; 15678 was dropped at the last step. Regex '!'.
per_probe.quote: Clear now: probe0=hashtag (+0.84, dominant), probe3=excl (+0.82, dominant), probe1=none.

decision_points.choice: Hand-coded regex extractors for 16 properties; kept the seven that split labels perfectly in every probe; greeting/sign-off/'honestly'/lowercase/sentiment dropped as freely varying
decision_points.quote: The curated property set (perfectly confounded with label in **every** probe) is exactly **7 binary properties**

decision_points.quote: Let me compute each latent's contribution to class separation (c_i = g_i · Δ_i) and find the important latents per probe.

Cross-probe sign templates of mean shifts (properties sit on different label sides in different probes) separate topic from property latents; sign-degenerate groups (he/present, list/brit/ps) split by corpus trigger tokens; pooled regression tried and abandoned

caveats: Probe-1 'none' rests on one flip-all pair; the probe-3 pair was built wrongly and not redone. The stage order of reading and shaping latent sets is approximate; exact hand-classification lists for groups are copied as constants, since they came from reading example tables. Probe 2's choice of list over P.S./exclamation was by elimination with weak evidence. load_public structure (samples dict keyed by probe) is assumed.
